desk.purpose: Editor background under the canvas sheet.

desk-deep.purpose: Gallery background and header. CSS var --desk-2.

chrome.purpose: rgba(24, 23, 22, 0.78) with 18px backdrop blur: top bar, sidebar, bottom bars, timeline.

chrome-solid.purpose: Selected segment, colour-well ring, icon on checked box.

sheet.purpose: rgba(30, 29, 28, 0.94): popovers, dialogs, panels, bubbles, toasts.

sheet-raised.purpose: Raised fill inside sheets. CSS var --sheet-2.

sheet-control.purpose: Buttons, fields, segmented track, blend chips. CSS var --sheet-3.

line.purpose: rgba(255,255,255,0.09): 1px borders, dividers, quiet hover fills.

line-strong.purpose: rgba(255,255,255,0.16): slider tracks, separators, thumbnail rings. CSS var --line-2.

ink-secondary.purpose: Resting icons, secondary text. CSS var --ink-2.

ink-tertiary.purpose: Labels, meta, units, ticks. CSS var --ink-3. The light-theme value measures about 3.4:1 on the light sheet at 11-12px: a known contrast defect in the build, not a sanctioned value.

chalk.purpose: The only accent: active, selected, primary.

headline.purpose: Sheet titles; dialogs step to 18px, the gallery empty state to 30px.

control.purpose: Segmented options, bottom-bar buttons, brush categories.

label.purpose: Sentence-case field and section labels in Ink 60.

numeric.purpose: Slider values, dimensions, percentages; always tabular.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Popovers, dialogs, panels, bubbles, toasts. Light theme: 0 18px 50px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18), 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1).

shadows.name: paper-cast
shadows.purpose: Gallery artwork; the editor canvas draws the same cast.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: House ease: entrances, chrome show/hide, switch knob, artwork lift.

motion.name: chrome-hide
motion.purpose: Hiding/showing the top bar and sidebar.

narrative.overview:
Atelier is a working surface, not a showcase. The artwork sits on a neutral mid-grey desk as a paper sheet with a soft cast shadow; everything else is graphite chrome, thin and translucent, pinned to the edges where a Procreate hand already reaches: a 46px top bar with navigation tools on the left and painting tools on the right, a floating pill sidebar for size and opacity, sheets that drop from the bar with a pointer notch. The interface recedes during long sessions and can be hidden entirely.

The one colour the chrome owns is tailor's-chalk yellow. It is a marker, not a paint: the 2px underline under the active tool, the tint behind the selected layer or brush, the primary action, a switch turned on, the text caret, the rotate handle of a transform. Sliders read as measuring tapes, ticked every 10%, and every number is set in tabular figures. Text hierarchy comes from ink opacity, not from hue or size jumps.

The chrome ships in two themes (graphite by default, a warm-paper light theme by preference); on-canvas overlays deliberately ignore the theme and are always drawn as a white-and-dark pair so they read over any pixel.
keyCharacteristics: Canvas first: chrome is translucent graphite (78% opaque, 18px backdrop blur) over a neutral grey desk.
One accent, chalk yellow, used only to mark state and the single primary action.
System UI face throughout; weight and ink opacity carry hierarchy; tabular numerals for all values.
Rounded, soft geometry: 9px controls, 12px sheets, pill sidebar.
Measuring-tape sliders with 10% ticks, vertical in the sidebar, horizontal in sheets.
Soft, diffuse shadows only on things that float over the canvas.

rules.name: The Chalk Mark Rule
rules.body: Chalk yellow marks what is active, selected or primary, and nothing else. At most one chalk-filled button per surface; every other chalk use is a line, a ring or a 16% wash.

rules.name: The Ink Tiers Rule
rules.body: Text hierarchy is three opacities of one ink (100 / 72 / 60), never a second text hue.

rules.name: The Theme-Blind Overlay Rule
rules.body: Anything drawn on the canvas itself (marching ants, brush cursor, lasso, crop, transform box and handles, clone target, eyedropper loupe) is a white stroke paired with a dark stroke or dark ring, regardless of UI theme, so it reads over any artwork.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number the user reads or scrubs (size, opacity, percent, px dimensions) uses tabular numerals so values don't jitter while dragging.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case at normal tracking; the chrome carries no uppercase, letter-spaced tags.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to surfaces that float over the canvas; bar-attached chrome gets a hairline and blur instead.

rules.name: The Frosted Chrome Rule
rules.body: Every translucent chrome or sheet surface carries backdrop blur (18px chrome, 20-24px sheets); translucency without blur is not allowed.

dos: **Do** keep chrome at the edges: top bar (46px), left pill sidebar, sheets dropping from the bar, contextual bars floating 14px above the bottom.
**Do** pair every translucent surface with backdrop blur and a 1px hairline border.
**Do** reserve chalk for active, selected and primary states; use the 16% Chalk Wash for selected rows and a 2px chalk line for the active tool.
**Do** tick every continuous slider at 10% intervals and set its value in tabular numerals.
**Do** draw on-canvas overlays as a white stroke paired with a dark stroke or ring, independent of the UI theme.
**Do** read every colour from the custom properties so the light theme follows automatically.
**Do** use the house ease `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` for entrances and chrome show/hide, and honour reduced motion.
**Do** keep the keyboard focus ring blue (`2px`, offset `2px`), distinct from chalk.
donts: **Don't** introduce docked panel stacks, a menu bar or a tool palette; tools belong in the top bar, sidebar, sheets and contextual bottom bars.
**Don't** add a second accent hue or use chalk as decoration, background or large fill beyond the single primary button.
**Don't** use hard or offset shadows; depth is soft and diffuse, and only for floating surfaces.
**Don't** add uppercase, letter-spaced labels or tags to the chrome.
**Don't** make chrome opaque over the canvas; the artwork should stay faintly visible behind bars and sheets.
**Don't** use Procreate's name, icons, brush files or other assets; the interaction model is shared, the identity is Atelier's.
